issues.legal_issue: A declaration of protected forest is effective whether issued after an inquiry or under an urgent procedure, and covers the declared area, including waste land.
material_facts: The State declared the relevant State-owned land to be protected forest by notification issued under the urgent procedure in the forest law.
The mines were granted leases or licences after the declaration.
The court-appointed committee identified the protected-forest areas using official maps and records.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was valid and effective, was not merely provisional, and covered the whole declared area, including any waste land within it. The exception preserving pre-existing rights did not assist mine operators whose leases or licences post-dated the declaration.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 29(1), (3) and (4) of the Rajasthan Forest Act, 1953, the State may declare State-owned forest land or waste land to be protected forest. Section 29 contemplates one effective notification, whether made after an inquiry and record or under the urgent procedure before their completion; the latter procedure does not make the notification provisional. Once declared, the distinction between forest land and waste land disappears. The proviso preserves existing individual or community rights, not rights acquired later. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.area_declared_protected_forest: The government declared an area to be protected forest.
predicates.declaration_included_waste_land: The declared area included land that was waste land.
predicates.mining_rights_granted_after_declaration: The government granted the mining rights after declaring the area protected forest.

issues.definition: When an area including waste land is declared protected forest and mining rights are granted afterward, the area is effective protected forest and those later rights are not saved.

issues.legal_issue: A court-appointed committee’s demarcation of protected-forest boundaries may be accepted when it is based on official records and maps and its identification of the areas is not disputed by its members.
material_facts: The court appointed a committee chaired by a former High Court judge and including senior State officials to identify the protected-forest areas.
The committee cross-checked Forest Department maps against Revenue Department maps and considered the relevant land records and material submitted by the parties.
The committee members agreed on the location of the mines and the protected-forest areas; their disagreement concerned whether mines in those areas should be closed.
Mine operators had an opportunity to participate in the committee’s exercise.
issues.conclusion: The court accepted the committee’s report identifying the protected-forest areas and the mines situated wholly or partly within them.
issues.legal_principle: The court relied on the committee’s elaborate examination of official maps and records, its composition, the participation of affected parties, and the absence of disagreement about demarcation. It considered the operators’ objections insufficient to displace that evidence. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this determination.

rule.if: environmental_writ_proceeding and court_appointed_demarcation_committee and committee_cross_checked_official_records and affected_operators_participated and committee_members_agreed_on_boundaries

predicates.environmental_writ_proceeding: A petitioner brought a proceeding seeking enforcement of environmental protections.
predicates.court_appointed_demarcation_committee: The court appointed a committee to identify the boundaries of protected areas.
predicates.committee_cross_checked_official_records: The committee compared official maps and records when identifying the boundaries.
predicates.affected_operators_participated: Operators affected by the proposed boundary identification had an opportunity to participate in the committee’s work.
predicates.committee_members_agreed_on_boundaries: The committee members agreed on the identification of the boundaries, even if they differed on what action should follow.

issues.definition: In an environmental writ proceeding, a court accepts a committee’s demarcation when the committee checks official records, affected operators participate, and committee members agree on the boundaries.

issues.legal_issue: Mining in protected forest is a non-forest activity that cannot be authorized without prior central approval, and mining operations in protected forest without that approval must stop.
material_facts: The committee identified mines situated wholly or partly within protected-forest areas.
The mining leases or licences for those mines were granted or renewed after the protected-forest declaration.
No prior approval or clearance from the Central Government had been obtained.
The court had earlier directed that mining not be carried on in the protected area.
issues.conclusion: The grants or renewals for mines in protected forest without prior Central Government approval were contrary to law. Mining in the wholly included mines had to stop, and mining in partly included mines had to stop to the extent the operations were within protected forest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2 of the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 requires prior Central Government approval for non-forest activity in forest land. Mining is a non-forest purpose, and a declared protected forest comes within the Act. Rule 4(6) of the Rajasthan Minor Mineral Concession Rules, 1986 also bars the grant or renewal of a mining lease in forest without the required Central Government clearance. The court also relied on its earlier direction barring mining in the protected area. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: environmental_writ_proceeding and mining_in_protected_forest and mining_is_nonforest_activity and mining_rights_granted_or_renewed_after_forest_declaration and not prior_central_approval

predicates.environmental_writ_proceeding: A petitioner brought a proceeding seeking enforcement of environmental protections.
predicates.mining_in_protected_forest: Mining operations were carried on wholly or partly within an area declared protected forest.
predicates.mining_is_nonforest_activity: The activity being carried on was mining rather than a forest activity.
predicates.mining_rights_granted_or_renewed_after_f: The government granted or renewed the mining rights after the area had been declared protected forest.
predicates.prior_central_approval: The Central Government gave approval before the mining activity was authorized.

issues.definition: In an environmental writ proceeding, mining in protected forest under rights granted or renewed after the forest declaration must stop if it is a non-forest activity and lacked prior central approval.

issues.legal_issue: Mining operations in a tiger-reserve area outside protected forest are subject to a prohibition requiring prior central permission, but may continue temporarily while operators seek that permission.
material_facts: The relevant mines were outside protected-forest areas but within the area identified as a tiger reserve.

A Central Government notification issued under the environmental protection law prohibited mining in the specified areas, including areas covered by the tiger-reserve designation, without prior permission.
The Central Government stated that the mine operators had not obtained prior permission.
The court allowed the mining to continue temporarily while operators sought permission and directed that it cease if permission was not obtained within the specified period.
issues.conclusion: Mining in mines outside protected forest but within the tiger reserve could continue for four months. Operators could apply to the Central Government for permission during that time; mining could continue thereafter only if permission was granted and subject to the Central Government’s orders. Without permission within that period, mining throughout the tiger-reserve area had to stop.
issues.legal_principle: The notification issued under Section 3 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, read with Rule 5 of the Environment (Protection) Rules, 1986, prohibited specified mining operations in the identified areas without prior Central Government permission. The court distinguished mines outside protected forest, whose original grants were not thereby necessarily illegal, from the prohibition imposed by the notification. No earlier case was relied on.

rule.if: environmental_writ_proceeding and mining_outside_protected_forest and mining_within_tiger_reserve and notification_requires_prior_central_permission and not permission_obtained

predicates.environmental_writ_proceeding: A petitioner brought a proceeding seeking enforcement of environmental protections.
predicates.mining_outside_protected_forest: The mines were outside the areas declared protected forest.
predicates.mining_within_tiger_reserve: The mines were within an area identified as a tiger reserve.
predicates.notification_requires_prior_central_perm: A binding notification prohibited the relevant mining operations without prior permission from the Central Government.
predicates.permission_obtained: The mine operators obtained permission from the Central Government to continue mining.

issues.definition: When mining is outside protected forest but within a tiger reserve, and a binding notification requires central permission that has not been obtained, mining may continue temporarily only while that permission is sought.

issues.legal_issue: Economic consequences do not justify allowing mining operations that are unlawful under enacted environmental and forest protections to continue.
material_facts: The mine operators argued that closure would affect investment, workers, the State economy, and mineral supplies.
The court found that the mining operations in protected forest lacked required approvals and that the environmental notification also prohibited mining in the relevant areas without permission.
The case concerned enforcement of enacted laws, rather than closure of an activity being carried on lawfully solely to advance competing ecological considerations.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the economic effects of closure did not permit the unlawful mining to continue and directed closure of the operations found to be illegal.
issues.legal_principle: The court reasoned that the Legislature and Parliament had already balanced economic and ecological interests in enacting the applicable protections. Where the activity is unlawful under those enactments, the court is enforcing the law rather than choosing to close a lawful activity based on a separate balancing exercise. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.environmental_writ_proceeding: A petitioner brought a proceeding seeking enforcement of environmental protections.
predicates.mining_found_unlawful: The court found that the mining activity violated applicable legal requirements.
predicates.economic_harm_from_closure: Closure of the mining operations would affect investment, workers, the economy, or mineral supplies.

issues.definition: In an environmental writ proceeding, economic harm from closure does not authorize mining that the court has found unlawful.

issues.legal_issue: A request to remove mining areas from protected forest in exchange for other land should be assessed before the court decides whether to permit the proposed removal.
material_facts: The State asked to have areas covering mines removed from protected forest and offered an equal extent of other land for inclusion.
The State’s proposal concerned only part of the listed mines, and some mines had already been closed.
The court did not decide the merits of the proposed removal and directed the Central Government’s environment and forest department to examine it and report to the court.
issues.conclusion: The court referred the State’s proposal to the Central Government’s environment and forest department for examination and a report, and deferred its decision on the State’s request until after considering that report.
issues.legal_principle: The court considered it appropriate to obtain the Central Government’s examination of the merits before ruling on the proposed alteration of protected-forest boundaries. It did not hold that the proposed removal was permissible. No earlier case was relied on.

predicates.environmental_writ_proceeding: A petitioner brought a proceeding concerning enforcement of environmental protections.
predicates.state_requested_protected_forest_exclusi: The State asked the court to remove an area from protected forest.
predicates.replacement_land_offered: The State offered other land for inclusion in protected forest in exchange for the proposed removal.

issues.definition: When the State seeks to remove protected-forest land and offers replacement land in an environmental writ proceeding, the request is referred for review before the court decides it.
